paper.title: Online convex optimization in the bandit setting: gradient descent without a gradient

settings.name_in_paper: Online bandit version of Zinkevich's model (bounded convex costs)
unmapped: cost functions are convex and take values in [-C, C] (not [0,1]); learner knows C
r B subset S subset R B: S contains a ball of radius r and is contained in a ball of radius R around the origin; learner knows R
learner has access to a Euclidean projection oracle onto S
settings.definition_quote: There is a fixed unknown sequence of convex functions $c_1, c_2, \ldots, c_n\cc S \rightarrow [- C,C]$, where $C>0$ and $S \subseteq \reals^d$ is a convex feasible set. The decision-maker sequentially chooses points $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n \in S$. After $x_t$ is chosen, the value $c_t(x_t)$ is revealed

settings.name_in_paper: Online bandit convex optimization with L-Lipschitz bounded convex costs
unmapped: cost functions are convex and take values in [-C, C]; learner knows C
r B subset S subset R B; learner knows R
learner has access to a Euclidean projection oracle onto S
settings.definition_quote: If we make an additional assumption that the functions satisfy an $L$-Lipschitz condition ... A function $f$ is $L$-Lipschitz if $|f(x)-f(y)| \leq L|x-y|$

symbols.C_f: bound on the absolute value of cost functions, |c_t| <= C
symbols.R_out: radius of a ball centred at origin containing S

conditions: r B subset S subset R B

source.label: thm:param
source.quote: For any $n\geq\left(\frac{3Rd}{2r}\right)^2$ and $\nu =\frac{R}{C\sqrt{n}}$, $\delta=\sqrt[3]{\frac{rR^2d^2}{12n}}$, and $\alpha=\sqrt[3]{\frac{3Rd}{2r\sqrt{n}}}$, the expected regret of $\mathrm{BGD}(\nu,\delta,\alpha)$ is upper bounded by $\E[\sum c_t(x_t)] - \min_{x \in S} \sum c_t(x) \leq 3 C n^{5/6}\sqrt[3]{dR/r}$.

results.notes: Oblivious adversary; expected regret against best fixed point in hindsight. Uses projection oracle onto (1-alpha)S.

conditions: r B subset S subset R B

source.quote: If each $c_t$ is $L$-Lipschitz, then for $n$ sufficiently large and $\nu =\frac{R}{C\sqrt{n}}$, $\alpha = \frac{\delta}{r}$, and $\delta = n^{-.25}\sqrt{\frac{RdCr}{3(Lr+C)}},$ $\E[\sum c_t(x_t)] -\min_{x \in S} \sum c_t(x) \leq 2n^{3/4}\sqrt{3RdC(L+C/r)}.$

conditions: S preprocessed into near-isotropic position (B subset T(S) subset 1.01 d B)
tuning: parameters of Theorem 2 with r'=1, R'=1.01d, L'=LR

source.quote: For a set $S$ of diameter $D$, and $c_t$ $L$-Lipschitz, after putting $S$ into near- isotropic position, the BGD algorithm has expected regret, $\E[\sum c_t(x_t)] -\min_{x \in S} \sum c_t(x) \leq 6n^{3/4}d\left(\sqrt{CLR}+C\right).$

results.notes: Statement mentions diameter D but bound uses R (the original containing radius). Preprocessing via Lovasz-Vempala runs in O(d^4) polylog time. Abstract/intro write sqrt(CLD) instead of sqrt(CLR).
